data.title: South Korea’s stablecoin push raises questions about a potential crypto rally
data.description:
The discrepancy between technicals and fundamentals isn’t exclusive to L1s anymore.

The stablecoin market is showing a similar trend this year. Technically, Tether’s USDT is down over 2.5% over the past 12 months. And with USDT accounting for more than 50% of the total stablecoin market, its outflows are still a major contributor to the stablecoin market’s almost $8 billion drop from its yearly opening market cap of $315 billion.

However, despite the outflows, stablecoin adoption has continued to gain ground. Notably, South Korea’s government and the Bank of Korea are planning to amend the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act this year to recognize stablecoins as payment instruments, underlining growing regulatory support around stablecoins.

To understand why this divergence matters, the aforementioned chart could give us a clearer picture.

According to DeFiLlama, OG stablecoins have been recording a continuous outflow of capital over the last 30 days, with Circle-issued USDC recording a total of 4.7% net decrease. On the other hand, newer products, such as RLUSD, BUIDL USD, USDf, and U, have been witnessing inflows. In particular, Falcon USD [USDf] registered a whopping hike of over 42%, pushing its market value above $1 billion.

Notably, this is where South Korea’s move matters. The recognition of stablecoins as a means of payment may stimulate their use and demand. Given that some new stablecoins have already gained popularity, favorable regulations may drive their adoption and popularity to even greater heights. Now, the big question is whether these newer players can turn growing adoption into sustained market growth. 

South Korea’s stablecoin push sparks debate over next crypto rally

South Korea’s stablecoin move is coming at a critical time.

Capital flows have been shifting, and unlike previous cycles where macro FUD sent investors to safe havens, gold and silver are under pressure. The spot price of gold was below $4,000/oz for the first time since 29th July, while silver was down 54% from its January all-time high and at its lowest since November. 

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has been performing reasonably well. In fact, at the time of writing, BTC was up more than 23% from its late July low of $65K, even though it’s still around 36.5% below its $126K peak.

Compared to gold and silver, BTC has been flashing signs of some relative strength too. The catch? The stablecoin market cap has fallen back to its July levels over the same window, and still seemed to be about 5% below its $321 billion peak.

In short, crypto has been holding up despite stablecoin liquidity weakening across the board. 

According to AMBCrypto, this is where South Korea’s move becomes important, as it adds to the growing gap between stablecoin adoption and market performance. BTC has exhibited resilience despite a drop in stablecoin market cap, suggesting that “adoption-driven” momentum could be supporting the market even as liquidity takes a hit.

Ultimately, South Korea’s support of stablecoins appears to be part of a broader market shift. Even though liquidity has been under pressure, rising adoption and growing interest in newer players suggests the market is evolving beyond its established leaders.

Combined with Bitcoin’s relative strength, this divergence might highlight how regulatory progress and adoption could shape the next phase of crypto market growth.

Final Summary

data.title: Senate Democrat probes Tether over alleged payments to ex-Trump crypto advisor
data.description:
Tether’s reported $6.8M payment to Nxum Group, co-founded by ex-White House crypto advisor Bo Hines, has drawn congressional scrutiny. 

According to Senator Richard Blumenthal, a ranking Democrat on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), the allegations raise ethics and corruption concerns.

For further clarity, Blumenthal asked Tether to clarify the alleged payments and potential conflict of interest by 3rd November. He wrote, 

Tether’s alleged multimillion dollar payment to a firm controlled by the White House official primarily responsible for cryptocurrency policy implicates federal ethics, anti-corruption, and lobbying laws.

Sen. Blumenthal wants Tether to submit all payments to Bo Hines, including the crypto wallet addresses used, between January and August 2025. The Senator also asked for documentation of all lobbying services Nxum offered Tether. 

Tether’s growing regulatory scrutiny

Bo Hines left the White House Crypto Council last August and was shortly hired by Tether as a strategic advisor. He now oversees Tether’s U.S operations. 

While serving as President Trump’s Chief Crypto Advisor, Tether reportedly routed payments through a third-party marketing firm called Notorious. Hines’ Nxum allegedly began getting direct payments after he left White House last August. Blumenthal also sought clarity on the arrangement with Notorious. 

In fact, some reports alleged that the payments by Tether were meant to seek more time to comply with U.S GENIUS Act provisions and keep its offshore operations. 

For its part, Tether acknowledged knowing the allegations,which were first reported by the Wall Street Journal in mid-October. However, the stablecoin issuer denied the claims, 

External counsel previously conducted an in-depth internal investigation into the matter, which found no evidence of wrongdoing.

Earlier in October, Blumenthal sought clarity on Tether’s relationship with Cantor Fitzgerald, the issuer’s reserve custodian. The Senator also pressed the Department of Justice (DOJ) to investigate Tether’s role in Iranian crypto illicit flows. 

Despite growing Tether scrutiny, however, USDT adoption has continued to rise, especially overseas. Total USDT users crossed 700M for the first time in Q3, translating to 6% quarterly growth. Over $70B or 39% of USDT supply is now dominated by savers, underscoring that the stablecoin goes beyond just payments.

Final Summary

  • Senator Blumenthal raised ethics and corruption concerns about Tether’s alleged $6.8M payments to ex-Trump crypto advisor Bo Hines. 
  • Tether denied the claims and any wrongdoing, citing an ‘in-depth internal investigation.’

data.title: How Quack AI’s 22% price crash puts Q’s $0.06 support in focus
data.description:
Quack AI [Q] suffered a deep market correction, losing 21.71% of its recent gains within 24 hours at press time, as its trading activity also weakened across the markets. The rapid price depreciation pushed Q to $0.09324, raising concerns about further losses.

The token’s trading activity also declined considerably, with its 24-hour spot volume dropping 22.44% to $26.41 million. This simultaneous decline in price and volume implied a weakening market participation as Q corrected from its recent highs, above $0.13 earlier in October.

As the sellers took over control, the downturn notably extended into the derivatives markets, as market participants also limited their exposure.

Q derivatives shrink as OI plunges

The derivatives market also registered a considerable contraction, which validated the broader decline in trading activity.

According to CoinGlass derivatives data, trading volume fell 17.70% to $161.63 million as of writing, highlighting limited participation in leveraged trading. On the other hand, the Open Interest (OI) dropped 32.21% to $37.05 million, suggesting a rapid reduction in prevailing futures positions.

Generally, such a significant decline, together with the falling prices, indicated that traders were closing positions instead of aggressively opening new ones. To be specific, leveraged long positions may have faced pressure during the decline, with long liquidations hitting $178.02K against just $17.13K in short liquidations.

Meanwhile, the reduction in prevailing positions additionally coincided with a notable shift in positioning among Binance’s top traders.

Binance top traders favor shorts over longs

Accordingly, Binance’s top trader’s Long/Short Ratio suggested a clear bearish bias as short accounts gained the upper hand.

At the time of writing, the short accounts accounted for 56.78% of top traders, while long accounts accounted for 43.22%, bringing the ratio to 0.76. This recent reading highlighted a notable departure from early October, where the long accounts consistently preserved the majority.

The ratio, in fact, previously climbed above 1.50 before declining rapidly during the second half of the month. Therefore, this shift reflected a  growing bearish sentiment among the top traders as Quack AI extended its price decline.

What do Q’s charts reveal?

Q’s daily technical structure highlighted a sharp price reversal after the token faced resistance around the $0.134327 area.

After several unsuccessful recovery prospects, the bears pushed the price below the $0.111600 level, flipping this former support into resistance. The recent daily candle notably extended losses towards the $0.088487 area, while its intraday low had reached $0.087900 at press time.

Meanwhile, the RSI indicator dropped to 57.62 as of writing, as it retreated from its previous overbought territory. Its decline below the RSI moving average of 75.55 further highlighted weakening buying strength.

Even though the indicator remained above the neutral 50 level, the steep downturn suggested that the bullish control was drastically weakening. The persistent selling pressure below the recent low therefore could deepen the price correction, potentially exposing the distant $0.060000 support unless buyers step in aggressively.

Final Summary

  • Quack AI’s 21.71% decline triggered heavy long liquidations as derivatives traders reduced their exposure. 
  • Q lost $0.1116 support, with a weakening RSI leaving further declines toward $0.06 possible.

data.title: FBI launches ‘Operation Blackout’ to dismantle global scam compounds — Details
data.description:
The U.S Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced “Operation Blackout” as a coordinated crackdown on international scam compounds that target American citizens through online fraud.

Instead of waiting for victims to lose money and then investigating individual cases, the operation aims to dismantle the criminal networks, physical facilities, and digital infrastructure used to run these scams.

The scammers’ spiderweb

According to a statement given by the FBI, these compounds operate across Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, functioning like entire towns with housing and other facilities.

They are allegedly controlled by criminal syndicates that use these operations to defraud people through fake investment platforms, online impersonation, and other digital schemes.

Remarking on the same, Director Kash Patel of the FBI said,

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, along with our partners at DOJ and the United States Attorney’s Offices, have seized over $17 billion from these scam compound fraud centers. Seized it. That means that’s money we got back.

The missing piece from the puzzle

Besides this, there are also ongoing efforts in Ghana and Nigeria. There, too, the authorities have reportedly arrested around 300 individuals and seized another $15 million linked to scams targeting American senior citizens.

Now, the key concern is that these compounds may also rely on human trafficking and forced criminal labor. Hence, it’s natural to assume that trafficked individuals can be confined and coerced into contacting potential victims online, while also persuading them to transfer money into fraudulent investment schemes.

Additionally, another concern is that dismantling compounds alone may not eliminate the threat. This, because criminal networks can relocate, rebuild their infrastructure, and continue operating across borders.

President Trump’s bold move against scammers

As expected, this update has coincided with a recent report from AMBCrypto, which highlighted how U.S President Donald Trump’s administration is intensifying its crackdown on overseas crypto scam networks.

So far, authorities have reportedly frozen nearly $1 billion in cryptocurrencies and have shut down over 500 fraudulent websites.

Patel praised President Trump for these efforts, stating,

There’s never been a president who has brought us together like President Trump has.

Final Summary

  • The FBI, along with partners at the DOJ and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices, has seized over $17 billion from these scam compound fraud centers.
  • Dismantling compounds alone may not eliminate the threat as criminal networks can relocate and continue operating across borders.

data.title: Can DASH crypto rally further after a 77% surge in Futures volume?
data.description:
Dash [DASH], the privacy cryptocurrency, has been on the rise, with the asset crossing over 10% in gains in the early hours of the 23rd of  October. Notably, market sentiment points to further upside for DASH as bullish momentum continues to build.

DASH bullish momentum strengthens

Based on recent movements in the Aroon and Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicators, chart analysis suggests that DASH may continue to rise.

At the time of writing, the Aroon indicator showed that the Aroon Up (orange line) had crossed above the Aroon Down (blue line), suggesting there has been more buying pressure.

Often, the greater the disparity between the Aroon Up and the Aroon Down, the stronger the buying pressure in the market.

Therefore, the market remains bullish, with a reading of 100.00% for the Aroon Up and 42.86% for the Aroon Down, confirming that bulls are still in control.

Additionally, the bullish outlook has intensified with the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), which has formed a bullish crossover, with the blue MACD line crossing above the orange signal line.

This classic bullish formation often attracts more buyers as investors continue to accumulate the asset.

Funding Rate and OI rise

Capital positioning in the perpetual market has hinted at why there has been a surge in DASH’s performance.

The Funding Rate, an indicator that tracks capital positioning in the perpetual market and categorizes it as predominantly long or short, shows that the former is the case.

The Funding Rate moved from the negative territory of -0.0080% to a high of 0.0056% as writing. A positive Funding Rate indicates that long positions outweigh short positions in the perpetual market.

Likewise, there has been a surge in capital inflows into the perpetual market as the Funding Rate turned positive.

Open Interest (OI) surged by over 16%, with an additional $14 million in fresh capital inflows, putting DASH’s total perpetual market capital at roughly $87.62 million as of this writing.

The surge in the Funding Rate and OI also points to investors rotating capital into DASH’s perpetual market as they anticipate a further rally.

DASH sentiment and volume improve

Sentiment and volume remain largely positive, as the consensus among investors is that DASH is likely to sustain its surge in the near term.

At press time, sentiment for DASH stood at 4.22, implying a strong bullish outlook and suggesting that investors are likely to keep accumulating the asset.

CoinMarketCap’s sentiment scale ranges from -10 to 10. When sentiment is significantly positive, as it is for DASH, there is a greater likelihood of the rally continuing.

Likewise, there has been a noticeable surge in volume. In the perpetual market alone, trading volume was up 77%, reaching $218 million. Volume and price rising at the same time strengthen the case for an asset sustaining its upward move.

Final Summary

  • DASH gained over 10% as the Aroon and MACD formed a bullish crossover, suggesting further upside potential.
  • DASH’s Funding Rate turned positive at 0.0056%, while Open Interest rose over 16% and perpetual trading volume climbed 77% to $218 million, pointing to increased bullish positioning.

data.title: Ethereum outflows hit 4-month high – Why ETH price still risks $2,300
data.description:
Ethereum [ETH] registered its largest daily exchange outflows in over four months, with 169,770 ETH leaving exchanges as market participants anticipate a potential price rebound. Santiment Intelligence is comparing the recent withdrawals to a similar spike recorded on the 5th of June.

Following that period, Ethereum recorded roughly 223,800 ETH in net outflows as its price reached a local bottom. Subsequently, the token staged a strong price rebound, making the later withdrawal spike particularly significant to the prevailing market conditions.

For context, substantial exchange withdrawals generally limit the amount of ETH readily available for immediate selling. Therefore, this recent development reinforced expectations of a possible price recovery, even though historical patterns sometimes offer no guarantee.

Meanwhile, selling activity among Ethereum’s earliest investors introduced another important  factor into the recovery story.

Ethereum OG whales cash out after years

According to Lookonchain, an early Ethereum investor reportedly sold 3,000 ETH valued approximately $7.23 million. Originally, the investor purchased the tokens nine years ago at just $18.83 each, which secured a reported 128-fold return.

Beside that, another Ethereum OG separately sold 1,000 ETH after acquiring tokens during Ethereum’s initial coin offering. This investor originally purchased 100,000 ETH at around $0.31 per token. The two long-term holders together sold 4,000 ETH, which highlighted renewed selling activity among Ethereum’s earliest investors.

Even though the reported exchange withdrawals implied limited available supply, the whale transactions showed continued selling among long-term investors.

Also notably, Ethereum’s derivatives market also highlighted persistent selling pressure, beyond these individual sales.

Futures sellers maintain control over ETH

As per CryptoQuant analytics, Ethereum’s Futures Taker CVD continued showing seller dominance, which implied sustained aggressive selling activity. In particular, this indicator measured the cumulative divergence between market buy and sell orders across the Futures markets of ETH.

The seller-dominant reading therefore  indicated that aggressive sellers continued outweighing buyers throughout the period observed. This derivatives positioning was in contrast with the considerable exchange withdrawals reported by Santiment.

Consequently, such positioning could likely invalidate recovery prospects, especially in case the aggressive Futures selling persists alongside the prevailing weak ETH price action.

Can Ethereum defend $2,300?

The daily timeframe chart highlighted continued weakness after ETH failed to sustain its earlier recovery toward the $2,540.68 price level. The altcoin subsequently pulled back toward $2,376.62, losing its key support at the $2,385.62 price level.

Notably, the latest candles highlighted repeated attempts to stabilize around this zone, but the bulls did not manage to establish a convincing rebound.

Meanwhile, the Parabolic SAR indicator remained above the prevailing market value at $2,509.93 as of writing, strengthening the current bearish structure.

Furthermore, the MACD indicator maintained a bearish crossover. Notably, the indicator’s negative histogram reading of -8.90 further validated that the bears retained the technical advantage.

Overall, the bearish technical indicators for now outweighed the bullish implications of exchange withdrawals. Unless the bulls reclaim the $2,385 support, ETH could face further price decline toward $2,300.

Final Thoughts

  • Ethereum’s exchange outflows reached a four-month high, but early investors continued selling their holdings. 
  • Persistent Futures selling and bearish indicators left ETH facing another potential decline toward $2,300.

data.title: GRAM crypto crashes 11% as long liquidations hit $5.8M – What’s next?
data.description:
Gram [GRAM], formerly Toncoin, fell 5.77% in the past 24 hours. On the 23rd of October, the altcoin’s price fell 11.08% in just one hour, from $1.30 to $1.15. Incidentally, this price dip was the first time GRAM fell below the $1.30 demand zone that has been kept intact since early August.

The price drop caused a cascade of long liquidations. CoinGlass liquidation data revealed that $5.83 million in long liquidations across all exchanges was recorded on Friday, compared to just $240.3k in short liquidations.

Buyer exhaustion at a key support zone combined with a liquidation cascade helped explain the recent GRAM losses.

How traders can capitalize on GRAM’s bearish bias

Toward the end of September, the altcoin rallied to a high of $1.74. Since it had also breached the $1.56 high made in August, it appeared to confirm a bullish price trend.

Strong derivatives and spot volumes back then, combined with bullish expectations for Bitcoin [BTC] as it rallied back above $80k, reinforced the positive GRAM outlook.

Since then, the market-wide buyer apathy led to a steep pullback for the altcoin. It dropped into the $1.30-$1.35 demand zone, highlighted in cyan. This region has been defended for nearly three months, but failed in the past 24 hours.

The A/D indicator highlighted a lack of buying pressure in recent days. The H4 MACD made a bearish crossover earlier in the week, drawing attention to the rising bearish momentum.

Moreover, swing traders should remain bearish because the price has decisively broken below both a key support zone and the previous swing low.

GRAM traders’ call to action: Sell the bounce!

The $1.30-$1.35 former demand zone is now a supply zone. GRAM could be oversold in the short-term and has the potential to bounce to this supply zone before another bearish impulse move.

Traders can wait for such a retest, and the next bearish crossover on the MACD, to look to go short. Meanwhile, a sustained recovery back above $1.36 would indicate a bounce that could reach $1.50-$1.60 before running out of steam.

Final Summary

  • GRAM, formerly Toncoin, saw an intense wave of selling that led to an 11% price drop within an hour of trading on Friday.
  • Heavy spot selling volume and a cascade of long liquidations helped fuel the swift price drop to $1.15, shifting swing traders’ bias bearishly.

data.title: Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $635M as BTC price tests $81K support
data.description:
Spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETF recorded its biggest outflows since June 2025 on the 22nd of October, 2026, worth $635.5 million.

On the same day, BlackRock’s IBIT led the withdrawals with $254.1 million. This was followed by Fidelity’s FBTC at $217.5 million, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB at $109.4 million, Bitwise’s BITB at $27.4 million, and Grayscale’s GBTC at $29.5 million.

In fact, together, these products accounted for the bulk of the daily outflow. Meanwhile, on the other hand, Morgan Stanley’s MSBT recorded a relatively small $2.3 million inflow that provided little offset to the broader selling pressure.

Trend reversal

The scale of the withdrawals was particularly striking because it erased the positive momentum built up during the preceding two sessions, which had collectively attracted more than $1.05 billion.

In fact, according to AMBCrypto’s recent report, Bitcoin ETFs recorded a massive $663 million in inflows, marking their largest single-day intake in two months.

At the same time, Switzerland’s FINMA approved a physically backed Bitcoin fund, BBIT, for retail investors, with trading expected to begin on the SIX Swiss Exchange in November.

Bitcoin is back near the $81K radar

This BTC ETF rollercoaster came as Bitcoin was trading at $81,612.79 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours but a drop of over 5% in the past month.

In other words, Bitcoin is once again back in the playground, where it is testing the $81,000 level. That said, Glassnode describes this price level as the estimated cost basis of investors in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.

For those unaware, the ETF cost basis refers to the average price at which investors acquired Bitcoin exposure through these funds. This level usually influences investor behavior.

So, if BTC remains above $81,000, the level could act as support and help stabilize the market. However, a sustained break below the $81K price level could weaken sentiment, particularly among investors who entered the market around this price.

Did altcoin ETFs mirror BTC ETFs?

On the other hand, other altcoin ETFs somewhat followed a similar pattern as BTC ETFs.

According to SoSo Value data, Ethereum [ETH] ETFs recorded $110.50 million in outflows, followed by Solana [SOL] ETF, which saw $8.51 million in outflows, and Hyperliquid [HYPE] ETF, which saw $7.88 million worth of outflows.

Notably, the newly launched Zcash [ZEC] ETF recorded $14.23 million in inflows, followed by the XRP ETF, which saw inflows worth $3.55 million all this on the 22nd of October.

Final Summary

  • BlackRock’s IBIT, Fidelity’s FBTC, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB, Bitwise’s BITB, and Grayscale’s GBTC accounted for the bulk of the daily outflow.
  • Bitcoin was trading at $81,612.79 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours.

data.title: MemeCore – How falling trading volume could derail M’s 11% rally
data.description:
MemeCore [M] has recorded an 11% price surge over the last 24 hours at press time, after a sharp rejection from the 20-day EMA at $1.13. Despite the surge, the token lacks volume, with its trading volume shrinking by 4% over the same period.

However, MemeCore derivatives are leaning to the bulls. The token’s Open Interest (OI) has gained by 28% to $6.8 million over the last 24 hours, and long positions account for 54% of the total leveraged position.

Could the positive derivatives keep the current momentum going? 

Rising OI supports bullish positioning

On the derivatives, most on-chain metrics are leaning to the bulls. MemeCore‘s OI has recorded a 33% increase to 34 million over the last 24 hours. The spike indicates that traders are opening or maintaining more outstanding derivatives positions. 

Moreover, the rise suggests growing interest in the token as its price rebounds.

At the same time, it’s key for investors and traders in running positions to note that long positions account for more than 54% of leveraged positions, giving bullish traders a modest majority. 

This positioning could support further gains if buyers continue entering the market and the price maintains its upward trajectory.

Falling volume raises questions

According to the recent data, MemeCore’s trading volume has slipped by 4% to $3.79 million over the last 24 hours despite the overall weekly volume surging significantly.

On the short term, the daily drop creates a divergence between MemeCore’s price action and market participation. While the token price has gained 11%, lower turnover suggests that fewer tokens are changing hands than during the previous 24-hour period.

If volume continues to weaken, the rally could struggle to attract enough demand to extend its gains out of the current ranging structure. The increase in OI may reflect growing speculative exposure rather than sustained spot accumulation.

Besides, this combination also raises liquidation risks. If the price reverses, leveraged longs could face forced closures, adding to selling pressure.

Can MemeCore extend its rally?

MemeCore’s short-term outlook depends on whether derivatives demand translates into sustained buying. A continued growth in OI, a stable long bias, and recovering spot volume would strengthen the case for further bullish push.

On the daily chart, the 11% rally shows renewed price strength and has pushed the token past the 20-day Exponential Moving Average, but declining volume limits confirmation.

Final Summary

  • MemeCore has gained by more than 10% after a sharp rejection around the 20-day EMA at $1.13, while trading volume slips 4%.
  • The network’s Open Interest climbs to $7.3 million, with longs accounting for 54% of leveraged positions.

data.title: Bitcoin sees $771M in whale withdrawals – Why BTC could reclaim $84K
data.description:
Institutional activity around Bitcoin [BTC] escalated as Fidelity and BlackRock received significant BTC transfers into their ETF wallets, suggesting fresh interest among these key asset managers.

According to Onchain Lens on X, Fidelity’s FBTC ETF wallet reportedly received 282.63 BTC valued around $23.08 million from Binance. Additionally, BlackRock’s ETF wallets also received 384.77 BTC, valued at approximately $31.4 million.

Combined, these transactions reflected a continued institutional activity despite Bitcoin’s latest price weakness.

Here it is important to note that even though wallet transfers alone could not validate fresh purchases, the movements strengthened the attention toward institutional Bitcoin positioning.

Beyond the institutional activity, another noteworthy accumulation activity emerged among newly created wallets.

Since the 1st of October, Bitcoin’s large holders additionally heightened their activity, with 40 newly created wallets withdrawing 9,458 BTC from Wintermute. These withdrawals totaled roughly $771.5 million, which reflected considerable movements among wallets potentially connected to large market players.

This concentration of withdrawals across the newly created addresses reinforced the chance of a well-coordinated accumulation ahead of a possible price recovery. In fact, such transfers often attract attention since investors sometimes move acquired Bitcoin into wallets for longer-term custody.

The broader exchange activity meanwhile provided additional context for assessing whether BTC holders were indeed reducing their available exchange supply.

BTC exchange withdrawals deepen amid reserve decline

Bitcoin‘s Spot market registered around -$465.55 million in Spot Netflows on the 22nd of October, validating the withdrawal narrative. For context, this negative netflow implied that more BTC left exchanges than entered during the reporting period.

Interestingly, Bitcoin’s USD-denominated exchange reserves fell 1.35% over 24 hours, reaching roughly $226.33 billion. These figures together pointed towards reduced exchange balances, even though Bitcoin’s valuation also influenced the dollar-denominated reserve metric.

Importantly, the continued withdrawals could reduce the immediately available selling supply in case holders continued moving coins away from trading platforms.

Now with institutional accumulation and whale withdrawals dominating the recent activity, Bitcoin’s price structure became increasingly important.

Bitcoin demand zone strengthens as SAR flips

Bitcoin’s daily timeframe chart highlighted buyers defending an important order block around the $81k price region.

Following the most recent price rebound, BTC traded around $81,764 at press time, maintaining its position above the identified demand region. Importantly, the Parabolic SAR had just flipped below price, with its dots visibly at $80,001, suggesting improving bullish conditions amid the earlier decline.

Meanwhile, the Money Flow Index (MFI) indicator stood at 53.74, implying moderately positive buying pressure as capital inflows slightly outweighed outflows. Overall, institutional transfers, whale withdrawals, and declining exchange balances favored a  bullish outlook as BTC defended its key support level.

Bitcoin, therefore, stands a better chance of extending its recovery toward $84,000 so long as buyers continue defending the demand zone supported by the bullish Parabolic SAR reversal.

Final Summary

  • Institutional Bitcoin transfers and $771.5 million in whale withdrawals highlighted growing accumulation activity.
  • BTC held its demand zone as the bullish SAR flip strengthened recovery attempts toward $84,000.
